task_name: Domino Delights BR Creative Validation Test Validity Review (INVALID - re-run after eligibility fix)
authoring_notes: Scored bands only (-1 to +1). Binary facts and actions live in rubrics_objective_compliance.json. There are no subtract-only penalty items in this task. The two behaviours that would otherwise have been penalties, inventing a figure with no source and letting post-2026-01-27 evidence move the verdict, are graded positively in objective compliance instead, so nothing is scored twice and nothing is scored only by deduction.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent separates the measurement problem from the creative question, so a growth lead reads the poor conversion rate and cost per install as an artefact of blocked installs rather than as a creative result.
rubrics.justification: The whole task turns on refusing the framing the room arrived with. This is the judgment call, not a fact lookup.
rubrics.evidence: The review explains that the numbers measure who could install, not which creative persuaded, and holds that line throughout.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Presents the runs as a creative read, ranks or grades the creatives on this data, or recommends replacing creative on the strength of it.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Notes the eligibility restriction somewhere but still discusses the figures as creative performance, leaving a reader unsure which reading holds.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: States the results are unreliable but does not explain that the metrics measure install eligibility rather than creative persuasion.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Draws the distinction explicitly and consistently: these runs measure install eligibility, the creative question is untested and stays open.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent handles the Spanish creative set and the Brazilian and Dominican audiences even-handedly, resting the read on the evidence that the restriction hit both language sets and that the Spanish run reproduced the English result.
rubrics.justification: The salient wrong answer here is a fairness failure dressed as analysis: a plausible-sounding conclusion that a language set or a market underperformed, drawn from data that could not measure either.
rubrics.evidence: The review declines to rank the language sets or the markets on this data and gives the reason in evidence terms.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Attributes the result to Spanish-language creative, to translation quality, or to Brazilian or Dominican audience or user quality.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Avoids the explicit claim but leaves the Spanish set or the markets under suspicion, for example by recommending they be reconsidered while the eligibility finding sits in a footnote.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: States both sets are untested but does not use the Spanish follow-up run as the evidence that rules out a language explanation.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: States both sets were equally blocked, cites the Spanish run reproducing the English result, and leaves the language and market questions genuinely open.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's re-run gate is conditional on verified prerequisites rather than on elapsed time, naming what has to be true before another run is worth paying for.
rubrics.justification: A lead has to know what unblocks the re-run. 'Retry next week' spends budget into the same defect; 'retry once eligibility is confirmed and event volume is fixed' does not.
rubrics.evidence: The review states the conditions for a valid re-run and ties them to the eligibility fix and the measurement defects.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Recommends re-running immediately or on a date, treating the restriction as already resolved.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Recommends a re-run without stating what must be verified first.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Conditions the re-run on the eligibility fix alone, leaving the event-volume and revenue-event defects out of the gate.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Names both preconditions, confirmed removal of the download restriction with a decision on the version floor, and corrected event volume and revenue-event mapping, before a re-run is worth funding.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's follow-up tickets are assignable slices with distinct owners' worth of work, covering eligibility confirmation, measurement integrity and the copy review, rather than a single catch-all item.
rubrics.justification: Objective compliance counts the tickets. This scores whether a lead could hand each one to a different team on Monday.
rubrics.evidence: Each child ticket states a distinct outcome and the evidence behind it, so it can be assigned without a follow-up conversation.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: One vague catch-all ticket, or tickets whose scope overlaps so much that ownership is unclear.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Tickets exist but state no outcome or no evidence, so an assignee would have to reconstruct the review.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Two of the three areas are assignable slices; the third is missing or too vague to act on.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Three distinct assignable children across eligibility, measurement and copy, each with its outcome and its evidence stated.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent marks the boundary between what the evidence establishes and what remains unknown, so the reader can see that the creative question, the true excluded-device share and the confirmation of the fix are all still open.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks for open questions to be carried rather than closed by inference. Overclaiming here is what turns a careful review into a false all-clear.
rubrics.evidence: The review carries the open questions as open, without substituting an estimate or an assumption for a missing figure.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Closes an open question with an unsupported inference, for example asserting how much of the Brazilian device base was excluded or declaring the restriction resolved.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Presents findings without distinguishing what is established from what is unknown.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Carries some open questions but treats at least one unresolved item as settled.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Names what is established and separately names the creative question, the excluded-device share and the unconfirmed fix as open.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent raises the denigrating ad copy as a brand and player-respect issue in its own right, separate from the validity verdict, without letting it dilute the main call.
rubrics.justification: The copy problem is real and worth flagging, but it is not why the test failed. Judgment is shown by keeping the two apart while raising both.
rubrics.evidence: The copy flag appears as its own item with its own follow-up and is not offered as an explanation for the poor conversion rate.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Presents the copy as the reason the test performed badly, or raises it only against the Spanish column.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Copy issue is absent, or mentioned so briefly that a reader would not act on it.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Raised as its own item but without naming the matched English and Spanish lines or without a follow-up.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Raised as a distinct brand and player-respect item, evidenced in both language columns, with its own follow-up and no bearing on the validity verdict.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent, when it cites a cost-per-install benchmark, states the scope that benchmark belongs to instead of treating it as a Domino Delights target.
rubrics.justification: The only written cost-per-install bar in the studio belongs to another title's half-year scorecard. Neither prompt asks for a benchmark, so an Agent that cites none is not penalised. An Agent that does cite one is judged on whether it scoped that benchmark correctly.
rubrics.evidence: A cited benchmark is reported with the scope it belongs to. If the Agent cites no benchmark, the item scores the baseline.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Presents the partner's 5 to 10 USD range as failing a Domino Delights target, or attributes another title's bar to Domino Delights.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: No benchmark is cited, or one is cited without either scoping it or misattributing it.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Cites the bar and signals it is not a Domino Delights target, without naming the title it belongs to.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Cites the bar, names its Zombie Match 3D scope (the page itself is titled as a 2025 half-year product objectives page, so either the title or the scope wording is acceptable), and states Domino Delights has no equivalent published target.
